Saab 1958: The GT 750 is the first Saab car fitted with seatbelts as standard.
Saab 1963: Saab becomes the first volume maker to offer diagonally split dual brake circuits.
Saab 1970: Saab introduces a world-first – headlamp wipers and washers.
Saab 1971: Heated front seats are introduced, the first time in the world they are fitted as standard.
Saab 1971: Saab develops the impact-absorbing, self-repairing bumper .
Saab 1976: Saab was the first manufacturer to produce a turbo engine with wastegate to control boost.
Saab 1978: Saab introduces another 'world-first,' the passenger compartment air filter .
Saab 1981: Saab introduces the split-field side mirror. This reduces the driver's blind spot.
Saab 1982: Saab introduces asbestos -free brake pads.
Saab 1983: Saab introduces the 16- valve turbocharged engine
Saab 1985: Saab pioneers direct ignition , eliminating the distributor and spark plug wires.
Saab 1991: Saab is the first manufacturer to offer CFC-free air-conditioning.
Saab 1991: Saab develops its ' Trionic ' engine management system, equipped with a 32-bit micro-processor.
Saab 1993: Saab introduces the ' Sensonic clutch ' and the ' Black Panel ', later to be called the 'Night Panel'.
Saab 1993: Saab develops the 'Safeseat' rear passenger protection system.
Saab 1994: Saab introduces the ' Trionic T5.5 ' engine management system, its processor is a Motorola 68332 .
Saab 1995: Saab presents an asymmetrically turbocharged V6 at the Motor Show in Frankfurt am Main , Germany.
Saab 1996: Saab introduces active head restraints , which help minimise the risk of whiplash .
Saab 1997: Saab introduces Electronic Brake-force Distribution
Saab 1997: Saab fits ventilated front seats to their new 9-5 .
Saab 2002: Saab unveils the second-generation Saab Active Head-Restraint system, known as SAHR2, in the new Saab 9-3 sedan
